reliability_evidence_label: Runtime and output confirmed; no availability
summary: BMW and Figure report substantial Figure 02 factory runtime and output, while the scheduled-time, downtime and intervention data needed to calculate availability remain unpublished.
finding: BMW corroborates 1,250 operating hours and 90,000 parts, but those totals have no scheduled-time, downtime or fleet denominator. BMW describes ten months of production support while Figure calls the broader program an 11-month deployment; the sources do not reconcile those scopes. Failure counts, intervention rate, MTBF, MTTR and measured availability remain unpublished.

summary: Digit performs a commercial tote-moving workflow at GXO, but the published duration and output milestones do not reveal operating availability or human-support frequency.
finding: The public record establishes a real commercial workflow, but its layers are uneven: GXO confirms the pilot, the commercial agreement is jointly announced, and Agility alone reports 100,000 totes and one year of full-time deployment. No source publishes operating hours, attempts, scheduled time, downtime, recovery time, autonomous-time share or intervention frequency, so availability and task success cannot be calculated.

summary: Walker S2's battery architecture is presented as enabling continuous operation, but no bounded field result demonstrates measured availability.
finding: Autonomous battery swapping may reduce energy-related downtime, but UBTECH's three-minute and 24/7 statements are capability claims, not field measurements. The reviewed sources publish no test count, swap-time distribution, failed swaps, operator observation window, scheduled time, runtime or maintenance interruptions.

summary: BMW confirms a Figure 03 logistics project and Figure shows the intended workflow, but no sustained production period or quantified operating result is public.
finding: BMW says Figure 03 will start work on a sequencing application; Figure calls its June material the first demonstration of that workflow at the plant. The sources do not establish a production start, observation window or continuous operating period, and publish no runtime, task volume, fleet size, intervention rate or reliability result.

reliability_evidence_label: Independent lab measurements; no field uptime
summary: Fraunhofer independently benchmarked a specified Unitree G1 configuration, producing laboratory measurements that characterize one test unit rather than field uptime or fleet reliability.
finding: Fraunhofer publishes useful measurements that reveal concrete operating constraints, including scenario-based power draw, derived per-charge endurance, actuator overheating and collision force. Availability is not applicable to this bounded laboratory benchmark because it defines no scheduled operating window; the tests also do not establish field availability, failure frequency, intervention rate or repair time. The public material does not report repeat counts or uncertainty for most tests.

context: Autonomous tote handling in electronics-factory logistics
summary: Siemens confirms a two-week HMND 01 factory test with throughput and task-success figures, but the published uptime wording lacks the denominator required for availability.
finding: The public record establishes a real factory test, 60 tote moves per hour and autonomous pick-and-place success above 90%. The reported ‘uptime exceeding 8 hours’ lacks scheduled time, downtime and event definitions, so it cannot be interpreted as an availability percentage or MTBF result.

location: Mark's store, Langley, British Columbia, Canada
reliability_evidence_label: Manufacturer-reported task count; no reliability rate
summary: Sanctuary reports a one-week retail pilot and 110 correctly completed tasks, without publishing the attempts, operating time or control mode needed to assess reliability.
finding: Sanctuary establishes that a general-purpose robot worked for one week at a Canadian Tire-owned Mark's store and says 110 retail-related tasks were completed correctly. The source does not identify the robot generation, distinguish unique task types from executions, publish failed attempts, or state whether the work was autonomous or teleoperated.

context: Heavy-component transport around an industrial washing process
summary: Schaeffler describes Digit performing a defined Cheraw factory task more than a year apart, without evidence of continuous operation or published reliability rates during that period.
finding: Schaeffler's own publications establish that Digit began a named material-handling task at Cheraw in early 2025 and was still handling heavy components there in April 2026. An independent factory report adds an eight-hour daily work pattern and roughly one-minute basket loop, but no source publishes cumulative runtime, scheduled time, downtime, interventions, failures or recovery. The calendar span and daily pattern therefore cannot be converted into uptime or MTBF.

deployment_status: Active factory pilot / production tasks reported
summary: BMW confirms a staged AEON factory pilot and Hexagon reports the start of production tasks, while runtime, task output, interventions and recovery remain unpublished.
finding: BMW confirms a staged AEON program at Plant Leipzig from laboratory evaluation through a December 2025 factory test and 2026 pilot integration. Hexagon later reports that AEON began production tasks on 12 June while still being trained, but does not identify a measured task volume or operating period. Runtime, scheduled time, downtime, interventions, failures, recovery, fleet size and availability remain unpublished; the product-level battery claim is not Leipzig operating evidence.

context: Intralogistics training and production-environment data collection
summary: Mercedes-Benz confirms Apollo training and data collection in a production environment, but does not publish autonomous task results, operating time or reliability measurements.
finding: Mercedes-Benz confirms that Apollo robots collected data in a real production-development environment at its Berlin-Marienfelde Digital Factory Campus. Employees taught production knowledge through teleoperation and augmented reality, and Mercedes says the robots are learning to act autonomously. A later Apptronik update names Mercedes-Benz within broader mixed teleoperation and autonomous data-collection workflows. None of the reviewed sources publishes operating hours, completed tasks, fleet size, autonomy share, intervention frequency, downtime, failures, recovery time or availability.

deployment_status: Completed prototype pilot / product deployment planned
location: Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America, Georgia, USA
summary: Hyundai confirms a completed Atlas prototype pilot for automotive parts sequencing, without publishing duration, output, intervention or reliability measurements.
finding: Hyundai confirms that an Atlas prototype completed pilot testing at HMGMA in October 2025 on a parts-sequencing workflow, and Boston Dynamics separately describes it as Atlas' first deployment. The public evidence identifies the site, task and prototype boundary, but publishes no duration, operating hours, robot count, task attempts, autonomous-time share, intervention count, failures, recovery or availability. Product-version specifications, 2026 RMAC shipment plans and Hyundai's 2028 production roadmap are tracked separately rather than attributed to the tested prototype.

deployment_status: Completed near-production PoC / successor deployment planned
context: Near-production bearing-ring bin-picking proof of concept
summary: Schaeffler confirms a completed pre-alpha proof of concept for bearing-ring handling, but no quantitative operating, task-success or reliability result is public.
finding: Schaeffler confirms that a proof of concept with Humanoid's pre-alpha robot was completed successfully, while Humanoid identifies the Erlangen site and a defined bearing-ring bin-picking workflow. The manufacturer also documents leader-arm teleoperation for training and claims autonomous regrasp correction. No source publishes the test duration, ring attempts, completed transfers, cycle time, throughput, test-mode autonomy, interventions, failures, recovery results or availability. Later Alpha/Beta deployment plans are kept separate from the tested pre-alpha system.

summary: ROSSMANN confirms one Walker S2 in a phased logistics pilot, while the reported task activity has no public runtime, output or reliability measurements.
finding: ROSSMANN confirms that it received one Walker S2 in Burgwedel on 17 March 2026 for a pilot planned across the full year. The operator defines the integration questions and intended work category but publishes no completed task result. UBTECH later reports material handling and sorting and claims the project demonstrated stability and viability, without definitions or measurements. The planned calendar window is not runtime, the distributor's several-dozen-unit purchase is not a ROSSMANN fleet count, and the battery-swap capability is not evidence of continuous operation.
